text:
alex: Heads-up — thinking about a lightweight "compact-on-access" layer to reduce long-tail fragmentation for tenant arenas. Idea: when a tenant's hotset is fragmented below X% contiguity, migrate hot slots into a fresh contiguous arena during idle windows.

jamie: curious, how do you plan to do the migration? GPU memcpy vs host staging?

alex: Two modes: intra-GPU memcpy if same device + no pinned constraints; otherwise staged via host pinned buffer. We'll throttle aggressively to avoid impacting p99.

nina: main concern is pointer stability for running sequences. We can't move backing pages out from under the KV cache without updating addresses atomically.

mohit: agree. We need an indirection layer: logical handle -> phys fragment. If we swap mapping atomically, runtime sees same handle. Cost is one level of indirection on lookup.

alex: exactly. Proposal: add "resident_handle" ABI: allocate_handle(A) -> (handle, frag_list). move_to_contiguous(handle, target_arena) updates mapping in single atomic op.

nina: implementation nit: atomic mapping update must be visible to tokenizer/kv cache readers. Can we use a small epoch counter + RCU-style read windows?

mohit: RCU or sequence-number stamp on the handle. Readers check stamp, retry if stale. It's cheap if retries are rare.

jamie: migration triggers: snapshot of access heat, if fragmentation_score > 40% AND compact_window_free_time >= 100ms. Add per-tenant rate limits.

alex: config sketch: ```
compact_on_access: {
  threshold_pct: 40,
  max_migrate_bytes_per_sec: 512000000, # 512MB/s
  idle_window_ms: 100,
  backoff_ms: 200
}
```

nina: what about costs during rollouts? If we compact while a model rollout is mid-flight, addresses might be in use by multiple versions. Need to pin versions or escalate to whole-model freeze.

mohit: option: compact only for pinned/non-shared arenas. For shared commons (e.g., base weights) skip compaction unless safe. We'll need a policy: tenant_private vs shared_readonly).
